title: The verse explained
hookLine: Ananda, Mahakaccana and Lomasakangiya each explain the same verse
last: SEE IT CLEARLY, RIGHT WHERE IT IS.

cards: Five hundred days. A line heard on day ten can come back differently on day four hundred. Same words, new weight.
The next three discourses take yesterday's verse and pass it through four monks. One teaches it from memory. Two first hear of it from a deity, and don't know it.
And one explains it when the Buddha leaves it unexplained. It's almost a study in how a teaching travels.

teach.h: ANANDA: HEARD IT AND KEPT IT
teach.b: In the hundred and thirty-second discourse, Ananda teaches the verse and its explanation to the monks in the assembly hall. The Buddha later asks who taught it, and confirms Ananda got it right.

Ananda had heard it and kept it. In the hundred and thirty-third, a monk named Samiddhi goes to bathe at some hot springs near Rajagaha. A deity appears at night and asks: do you know the bhaddekaratta verse?
No. Learn it, says the deity. So Samiddhi asks the Buddha, who recites only the verse and goes inside.
The monks are left with a short poem and no explanation.
They go to Mahakaccana, known for unpacking the Buddha's brief sayings.
He explains it through the senses: you chase the past when your mind is bound by desire to what the eye once saw, thinking, such was my eye, such were the sights.
You build on the future when you set your heart on what the eye will see. The Buddha hears this and says: if you'd asked me, I'd have explained it the same way.

In the hundred and thirty-fourth, a monk named Lomasakangiya is asked about the verse by a deity named Candana. He doesn't know it. But Candana does, and recites it, saying the Buddha once taught it to the gods.
So Lomasakangiya walks all the way to Savatthi to hear it properly.
Three discourses, three ways of meeting the same few lines, and one line they all carry: do today what needs doing, with energy.
In Pali, ajja eva kiccam atappam: today itself, the ardent effort.

how: Buddhist monastics memorize and chant short verses and study the commentaries that explain them; the bhaddekaratta verse is among those chanted in some communities.

o: a vow kept for a whole lifetime
a calm that needs no effort

games.q: one verse, four monks: tap the pairs.
p: taught it in the assembly hall
asked by a deity at the hot springs
walked to Savatthi to learn it

s: the Buddha says Mahakaccana explained the verse wrongly
he says if they'd asked him, he would have explained it the same way.
in MN 134 a deity knows the verse when the monk doesn't
Candana recites it and says the Buddha taught it to the gods.
the Buddha explains the verse himself every time
in MN 133 he recites only the verse and goes inside, leaving Mahakaccana to explain it.

games.q: the Buddha recites a short verse and goes into his dwelling without explaining it. you're one of the monks. what do the monks in MN 133 do?
o: go to Mahakaccana and ask him to explain it.
games.why: they go to Mahakaccana, known for expanding the Buddha's brief sayings, and the Buddha approves his explanation.

practice: Silently and slowly, say a short version of the verse in your own words, to keep it the way Ananda kept his, one line with each out-breath: don't chase the past; don't pin hopes on the future; see what's here; today, the effort.
Then rest in whatever is actually here between the lines.

wordCard.voice: Atappa. Ardor, keen effort: the line that Ananda, Mahakaccana and Lomasakangiya each carried on, as they met the bhaddekaratta verse. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali atappa: ardor, keen effort. from the verse: today itself, the ardent effort.

carryVoice: Your line: today, the effort. Five hundred days in, the effort is still only ever today's. Day five hundred, done.
